supplementalSources.name: PHSA CHSA v2018 Health Profiles
supplementalSources.scope: Original profile geography vintage and exact latest source dashes; profile/database precision reconciliation.

notes: Supplementary public measurements retrieved directly from BCCDC/PHSA on 12 October 2026. They were not present as CHSA scientific rows in the collected Zoer C016 CSV; C016 only supplies related inventory context.

Native CHSA identifiers, names and hierarchy match the source profile’s 2018 boundary configuration. The map uses the archived Ministry geometry mirrored by Community Map of Canada, not PGMaps current 2022 polygons. McBride/Valemount remains one 2018 area; its value is not split between later McBride and Valemount areas.

The two views retain eight original indicators, Total only, over FY 2001.2002 through FY 2020.2021. A normalized display period retains the fiscal duration. October 2026 retrieval does not make these rates current.

Rates use the 2011 Canadian Census population for age standardization. They are published administrative-registry measures per 1,000, not raw cases or crude percentages. Incidence and lifetime prevalence have separate definitions, retained with the original notes and further-information link.

Asthma and diabetes use ages 1+, COPD ages 35+, and hypertension ages 20+. Different age universes limit cross-condition rankings. Select one indicator and fiscal period for one value per CHSA; rates are not additive across places or conditions.

The database download omits 187 potential indicator/year cells among the 29 listed Northern CHSAs. Six latest missing cells have explicit profile CSV dashes and remain null; other absent historical cells remain absent. The dash does not specify its particular non-release reason. Neither omissions nor unreleased communities are assigned zero.

Forty Northern v2018 context polygons include 29 publicly listed measured CHSAs. The portal excludes publicly identifiable Indigenous CHSAs; no restricted values are requested or reconstructed. This public subset cannot supply a complete Northern total.

The source warns that small numerator or denominator counts can create volatility and obscure trends. Confidence intervals are not provided in these downloads. Rates do not establish trial eligibility, service demand, causal changes or NHHR effects, and are not multiplied by population projections to infer cases.

Database rates retain their reported one-decimal precision. The 226 reported latest cells reconcile with the higher-precision profile literals within the source rounding interval; those profile literals are verification evidence rather than replacement series values.
Copyright © 2026 Provincial Health Services Authority. Source designations and profile URLs are retained in the records and exports; see PHSA terms of use and the portal’s data-download guidance.

Asthma age-standardized incidence rate p.definition: Asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease of the airways that is characterized by wheezing, coughing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath. A case is defined as one hospitalization or two physician visits in one year, or 1 physician visit with an Asthma diagnostic code [ICD-9 (493), ICD-10 (J45)] and 2 Asthma prescriptions in 1 year. The case definition applies to persons aged 1 and older.
Asthma age-standardized incidence rate p.notes: The 2011 Canadian Census population was used for age standardization. Incidence rate is the rate at which new cases of disease occur in a specified population during a specified time period. It is calculated as the number of new cases in the at-risk population in the specified period of time divided by the person-time at risk or the number of persons at risk (i.e., mid-year population in a reporting year minus previous year's prevalent cases) in the same period.
Asthma age-standardized incidence rate p.comments: Variability of counts due to small numbers in individual age/sex cells, or in totals, for either numerator or denominator may cause year to year volatility in rates and make trends difficult to interpret or identify.

Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (C.definition: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) includes a number of diseases such as chronic bronchitis and emphysema. These diseases are non-reversible and entail the narrowing of the airways that limits air flow to and from the lungs. Many cases are caused by smoking, or exposure to smoke, and some may be associated with occupational exposure (Provincial Health Officer's Annual Report, 2009). A case is defined as one hospitalization or two physician visits in one year and coded with a COPD-related diagnostic code [ICD-9 (491,492, 496), ICD-10 (J41-J44)]. The case definition applies to persons aged 35 and older.
Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (C.notes: The 2011 Canadian Census population was used for age standardization. Incidence rate is the rate at which new cases of disease occur in a specified population during a specified time period. It is calculated as the number of new cases in the at-risk population in the specified period of time divided by the person-time at risk or the number of persons at risk (i.e., mid-year population in a reporting year minus previous year's prevalent cases) in the same period.
Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (C.comments: Variability of counts due to small numbers in individual age/sex cells, or in totals, for either numerator or denominator may cause year to year volatility in rates and make trends difficult to interpret or identify.

Diabetes Mellitus age-standardized incid.definition: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic condition that results from the body's inability to sufficiently produce or use insulin (a hormone produced by the cells in the pancreas that regulates the storage and use of glucose in the body). (Provincial Health Officer's Annual Report, 2005). A case is defined as one hospitalization  or two physician visits in one year with specified diagnostic code(s) [ICD-9 (250), ICD-10 (E10, E11, E13, E14)]; or two or more insulin prescriptions in one year; or two or more oral antihyperglycemic (not including metformin) prescriptions in one year; or one insulin and one oral antihyperglycemic (including metformin) in one year; or 2 metformin prescriptions and 1 physician visit in one year with the specified ICD code(s).  The case definition applies to persons aged 1 and older.
Diabetes Mellitus age-standardized incid.notes: The 2011 Canadian Census population was used for age standardization. Incidence rate is the rate at which new cases of disease occur in a specified population during a specified time period. It is calculated as the number of new cases in the at-risk population in the specified period of time divided by the person-time at risk or the number of persons at risk (i.e., mid-year population in a reporting year minus previous year's prevalent cases) in the same period.
Diabetes Mellitus age-standardized incid.comments: Variability of counts due to small numbers in individual age/sex cells, or in totals, for either numerator or denominator may cause year to year volatility in rates and make trends difficult to interpret or identify.

Hypertension age-standardized incidence.definition: Hypertension (high blood pressure) is an important risk factor for heart disease and stroke and also a co-morbidity of diabetes. The combination of poorly controlled blood pressure and blood sugar is particularly dangerous (Provincial Health Officer's Annual Report, 2009). A case is defined as one hospitalization or two physician visits in two years with specified diagnostic code(s) [ICD-9 (401, 402, 403, 404, 405), ICD-10 (I10, I11, I12, I13, I15)].  The case definition applies to persons aged 20 and older.
Hypertension age-standardized incidence.notes: The 2011 Canadian Census population was used for age standardization. Incidence rate is the rate at which new cases of disease occur in a specified population during a specified time period. It is calculated as the number of new cases in the at-risk population in the specified period of time divided by the person-time at risk or the number of persons at risk (i.e., mid-year population in a reporting year minus previous year's prevalent cases) in the same period.
Hypertension age-standardized incidence.comments: Variability of counts due to small numbers in individual age/sex cells, or in totals, for either numerator or denominator may cause year to year volatility in rates and make trends difficult to interpret or identify.

datasets.title: Northern CHSA lifetime disease prevalence
datasets.description: Direct historical public registry rates at 29 Northern community health service areas, preserving source v2018 geography, definitions and missingness.
datasets.timeLabel: FY 2001–2002 through FY 2020–2021 · CHSA v2018 · retrieved 12 October 2026
datasets.sourceName: BC Ministry of Health via BCCDC / PHSA Community Health Data
datasets.tableName: PHSA General Health topic / CDR2022 / SearchByLocationDownload CHSA CSVs and six explicit profile markers

supplementalSources.name: PHSA General Health topic (CDR2022)
supplementalSources.scope: Direct public CHSA CSV measurements, Total only, original FY2001–2002 to FY2020–2021; retrieved 12 October 2026.

supplementalSources.name: PHSA CHSA v2018 Health Profiles
supplementalSources.scope: Original profile geography vintage and exact latest source dashes; profile/database precision reconciliation.

notes: Supplementary public measurements retrieved directly from BCCDC/PHSA on 12 October 2026. They were not present as CHSA scientific rows in the collected Zoer C016 CSV; C016 only supplies related inventory context.

Native CHSA identifiers, names and hierarchy match the source profile’s 2018 boundary configuration. The map uses the archived Ministry geometry mirrored by Community Map of Canada, not PGMaps current 2022 polygons. McBride/Valemount remains one 2018 area; its value is not split between later McBride and Valemount areas.

The two views retain eight original indicators, Total only, over FY 2001.2002 through FY 2020.2021. A normalized display period retains the fiscal duration. October 2026 retrieval does not make these rates current.

Rates use the 2011 Canadian Census population for age standardization. They are published administrative-registry measures per 1,000, not raw cases or crude percentages. Incidence and lifetime prevalence have separate definitions, retained with the original notes and further-information link.

Asthma and diabetes use ages 1+, COPD ages 35+, and hypertension ages 20+. Different age universes limit cross-condition rankings. Select one indicator and fiscal period for one value per CHSA; rates are not additive across places or conditions.

The database download omits 187 potential indicator/year cells among the 29 listed Northern CHSAs. Six latest missing cells have explicit profile CSV dashes and remain null; other absent historical cells remain absent. The dash does not specify its particular non-release reason. Neither omissions nor unreleased communities are assigned zero.

Forty Northern v2018 context polygons include 29 publicly listed measured CHSAs. The portal excludes publicly identifiable Indigenous CHSAs; no restricted values are requested or reconstructed. This public subset cannot supply a complete Northern total.

The source warns that small numerator or denominator counts can create volatility and obscure trends. Confidence intervals are not provided in these downloads. Rates do not establish trial eligibility, service demand, causal changes or NHHR effects, and are not multiplied by population projections to infer cases.

Database rates retain their reported one-decimal precision. The 226 reported latest cells reconcile with the higher-precision profile literals within the source rounding interval; those profile literals are verification evidence rather than replacement series values.
Copyright © 2026 Provincial Health Services Authority. Source designations and profile URLs are retained in the records and exports; see PHSA terms of use and the portal’s data-download guidance.

Asthma age-standardized lifetime prevale.definition: Asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease of the airways that is characterized by wheezing, coughing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath. A case is defined as one hospitalization or two physician visits in one year, or 1 physician visit with an Asthma diagnostic code [ICD-9 (493), ICD-10 (J45)] and 2 Asthma prescriptions in 1 year. The case definition applies to persons aged 1 and older.
Asthma age-standardized lifetime prevale.notes: The 2011 Canadian Census population was used for age standardization. Lifetime prevalence is the proportion of individuals who have had the condition for at least part of their lives at any time during their life course. In BC Chronic Disease Registry, this refers to the proportion of residents who were diagnosed/identified as a case at least once and were still alive and residing in the province during a reporting time period (fiscal year). Once the case definition criteria are met in a year, cases are then carried forward to count as a case every year thereafter until the person's death, their migration out of BC, or the absence of follow-up.
Asthma age-standardized lifetime prevale.comments: Variability of counts due to small numbers in individual age/sex cells, or in totals, for either numerator or denominator may cause year to year volatility in rates and make trends difficult to interpret or identify.

Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (C.definition: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) includes a number of diseases such as chronic bronchitis and emphysema. These diseases are non-reversible and entail the narrowing of the airways that limits air flow to and from the lungs. Many cases are caused by smoking, or exposure to smoke, and some may be associated with occupational exposure (Provincial Health Officer's Annual Report, 2009). A case is defined as one hospitalization or two physician visits in one year and coded with a COPD-related diagnostic code [ICD-9 (491,492, 496), ICD-10 (J41-J44)]. The case definition applies to persons aged 35 and older.
Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (C.notes: The 2011 Canadian Census population was used for age standardization. Lifetime prevalence is the proportion of individuals who have had the condition for at least part of their lives at any time during their life course. In BC Chronic Disease Registry, this refers to the proportion of residents who were diagnosed/identified as a case at least once and were still alive and residing in the province during a reporting time period (fiscal year). datasets.mapBoundaryCaption: CHSA boundary version 2018: BC Ministry of Health geometry via the Community Map of Canada ArcGIS mirror, reviewed 12 October 2026. Shared-topology display simplification: 50 m. The mirror is licensed for mapping/visualization only; no spatial analysis or allocation is performed. Forty Northern context polygons include 29 publicly listed measured CHSAs. Unreleased communities are not assigned zeros. The legacy official DataBC ZIP is unavailable; no fresh official ZIP verification is claimed.
